goal: Make performance history complete and truthful across every transfer topology, then use trustworthy prior results to warm-start adaptive concurrency so repeat transfers become fast sooner before the next release.
recommended_approach: Record orthogonal topology, local role, peer identity, and confidence-qualified controller outcomes at the unified session boundary; persist them through a serialized, service-aware store that profile and diagnostics can query; negotiate receiver-clamped initial stream seeds across the session wire; and let both controllers re-explore upward or downward with cold-start fallback before proving every topology and stale-seed case in integration and rig A/B tests.
comparison: The reviewed plan correctly favors unified-session instrumentation, schema migration, route-separated reporting, advisory seeds, and retirement of the unused predictor. It is not yet the best approach because its no-wire constraint conflicts with epoch-zero negotiation, its per-user store cannot provide the promised daemon-inclusive view in documented service deployments, the checker controller cannot recover below a high seed, and its route model omits or collapses supported topology and role distinctions.
material_changes: Permit explicit session negotiation of a preferred initial stream count, clamped by receiver capacity, or redefine ph-5 as post-open accelerated ramping and change its acceptance criterion accordingly.
Define a writable daemon-owned store plus a supported query/toggle path that lets profile and diagnostics include daemon records; serialize concurrent writes and compact atomically.
Redesign seeded AdaptiveCheckers to search downward from an excessive seed, and persist seeds only after sufficient evidence that the controller actually settled.
Model topology and local data role separately, including remote-to-remote delegation and daemon source versus daemon destination, and test every recording call site.

findings.title: ph-5 cannot warm-start epoch zero without changing the session contract
findings.evidence: docs/plan/PERF_HISTORY_PLANNING.md:38 - The plan forbids wire/proto changes while lines 72-73 require a seeded worker count at session open; crates/blit-core/src/transfer_session/data_plane.rs:118 validates every epoch-zero grant against receiver_initial_streams, and lines 189-198 always grant that conservative floor.
findings.predicted_failure: A learned count above the floor cannot be honored at session open: changing it locally causes a protocol violation, while applying it through later ADD epochs is not the promised warm start and retains the convergence delay.
findings.better_approach: Add a defaultable preferred-initial-streams negotiation field, clamp and acknowledge it at the receiver, bump the contract version, and test both initiator-role layouts; otherwise explicitly scope the feature to rapid post-open resizing.

findings.title: Daemon records will not be visible or controllable through the promised local reports
findings.evidence: docs/plan/PERF_HISTORY_PLANNING.md:54 - The daemon is assigned the same user-config-dir store and toggle; crates/blit-core/src/config.rs:25 resolves that directory from the current process user, while docs/DAEMON_CONFIG.md:449 runs the documented Linux service as User=blit under ProtectSystem=strict and ProtectHome=read-only.
findings.predicted_failure: The daemon may be unable to append at all under the documented service sandbox; if it can append, it writes the service account's store while an operator's blit profile and diagnostics commands read and toggle a different user's store, so daemon-served transfers remain missing and disable does not control them.
findings.better_approach: Give the daemon an explicitly writable service data directory and expose authenticated query, clear, and enablement operations to the existing reporting surface, merging client and daemon records with origin labels.

findings.title: The existing checker policy cannot unwind an excessively high historical seed
findings.evidence: docs/plan/PERF_HISTORY_PLANNING.md:46 - The design requires any bad seed to walk back down; crates/blit-core/src/transfer_session/checkers.rs:111 treats the first observation as a baseline and probes upward, while lines 130-142 can only undo that last probe before permanently settling.
findings.predicted_failure: With a stored seed of 32 for a destination whose new optimum is 4, the controller probes 64, returns to 32 on regression, and settles there; the stale seed remains substantially worse than cold-start behavior.
findings.better_approach: Use bidirectional bracketing around a seed, continuing downward while throughput improves, and only overwrite a seed after a minimum sample count and an explicit settled-confidence condition.

findings.title: The proposed route field cannot represent every supported transfer without mixing unlike roles
findings.evidence: docs/plan/PERF_HISTORY_PLANNING.md:91 - The schema offers only local, remote_push, remote_pull, and daemon_served, and lines 116-119 list only three missing call sites; crates/blit-core/src/transfers/dispatch.rs:65 has a separate RemoteToRemoteDelegated route, while crates/blit-daemon/src/service/core.rs:395 already distinguishes daemon push and pull roles.
findings.predicted_failure: Delegated remote-to-remote runs driven by the CLI are omitted, and daemon-source and daemon-destination measurements are aggregated together as daemon_served, producing misleading reports and potentially contaminating seed selection.
findings.better_approach: Store orthogonal topology, local role, and control initiator fields, then cover local-local, push, pull, both delegated daemon participants, and the delegated coordinator in an explicit recording matrix.

findings.title: The current capped JSONL writer is unsafe for daemon concurrency
findings.evidence: crates/blit-core/src/perf_history.rs:481 - Rotation checks file length and then truncates the live file with File::create at line 486 without locking or atomic replacement; crates/blit-daemon/src/service/core.rs:417 spawns each served transfer independently.
findings.predicted_failure: Concurrent session completions can append between the final length check and truncation, or run overlapping rotations, losing valid records and seeds or leaving malformed JSONL that readers silently skip.
findings.better_approach: Route daemon completions through one writer actor or use an interprocess lock, and compact by writing and syncing a temporary file followed by atomic replacement while preserving appends.
